summary.title: #define CTO
summary.one_liner: Greg Brockman's account of how Stripe hired a VP Engineering to take over people management, which let him redefine his CTO role and return to writing code.
keywords: head of infrastructure vs head of product
takeaways: Hiring a VP Engineering took over 1:1s and recruiting, which let the CTO shift focus away from daily people problems.
Delegation works best when the executive is fully out or deeply involved in one area; 'sparse micromanagement' (overturning decisions then disappearing) is the worst option.
A CTO can get organizational visibility through doing the work, talking to many people, observing work, or planning, and coding again gave the author the best feedback loop.
Frequent, regular one-on-ones between the CTO and VP Engineering helped them align and build a working model of each other's reactions.
Most CTOs the author surveyed acted as facilitators of the technology organization rather than chief architect.
summary.summary: Greg Brockman, Stripe's CTO, describes how he went from an early engineer doing infrastructure, culture and recruiting work to a formal CTO role. He recounts recruiting Marc Hedlund as VP Engineering, including a multi-day interview process and how the two divided responsibilities. The post then covers how he defined his role after surveying about 20 CTOs and VPs, and why he returned to writing code to regain visibility into the organization. It is a first-person experience report rather than a how-to guide.
